text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with one quote of every variant type for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: The Harrowfield Vocational Training Centre opened in 2016 to serve young people aged 18 to 24 in the eastern wards of Lenmouth. Since then, 1,240 trainees have completed courses in welding, tailoring, solar installation and motorbike repair. Youth unemployment in the district stands at 38 percent, nearly double the national rate. Employers consulted during our 2023 market scan reported that most applicants did not have the practical skills required for entry-level work. Graduates of the centre, by contrast, found paid employment within six months in 62 percent of cases. However, the centre has never had the funds to offer job placement support beyond the final week of training, and female enrolment remains low at one in five trainees.

passages.source_passage: Before your first visit to a farmer group in Ostava Valley, make sure you have read the seed calendar for the season. The Greenmere Drylands Project distributes three drought-tolerant varieties: short-cycle sorghum, pearl millet and cowpea. Each household receives 4 kilograms of seed and a printed planting card. Do not promise farmers that these crops will survive every dry spell; in 2022, yields still fell by 30 percent in the driest villages. Encourage farmers to plant after the first 20 millimetres of rain, not before. Volunteers should record germination rates two weeks after sowing and share them with the field coordinator. If a farmer reports pests, never recommend chemical sprays yourself.

passages.source_passage: This mid-term evaluation covers the first 18 months of the Little Steps Playgroup Network across the hill districts of Varonne. By March 2024, 46 playgroups were meeting weekly, against a target of 60. Attendance averaged 14 children per session, and caregiver participation was higher than expected. Facilitators reported that fathers rarely attended, and in nine groups no male caregiver had joined a single session. Developmental screening found that 71 percent of enrolled children met age-appropriate language milestones, compared with 54 percent at baseline. The evaluation team did not find evidence that play materials were being shared between groups as planned. Recommendations include a refresher training for facilitators and a dedicated outreach strategy for fathers.

passages.source_passage: The Kestrel Lane Literacy Circles began in 2019 as a single evening class in a church hall in Brisford. Today the network runs 12 classes across four neighbourhoods, each meeting twice a week from 6 to 8 p.m. An estimated 22 percent of adults in these neighbourhoods cannot read a medication label or a tenancy agreement. Most learners are women working daytime shifts who could not attend school as children. Experienced learners often mentor newcomers in the first month. Of the 310 learners enrolled last year, 188 progressed at least one reading level. Volunteer tutors are not paid, and turnover is high: half leave within their first year. This proposal seeks support to train paid lead tutors and to provide childcare during sessions.

passages.source_passage: Midway through the Sefa Basin Net Campaign, distribution teams had delivered 84,500 long-lasting insecticidal nets to households in 37 villages. This represents 68 percent of the target set for December 2024. Household surveys in a sample of 600 homes found that nets were hanging over sleeping spaces in most visited homes. However, enumerators observed that children under five were not always sleeping under a net, particularly in households with more than six members. Teams did not reach the island settlements on Lake Oru during the rainy season because boats were unavailable. Reported malaria cases at the two district clinics fell by 19 percent compared with the same quarter last year. The evaluators caution that this decline cannot yet be attributed to the campaign alone.

passages.source_passage: During the 2023 school year, the Becas Luminar programme supported 215 girls attending secondary schools in the department of San Arelio. Each scholarship covered tuition, uniforms and a monthly transport allowance of 25 dollars. Retention was strong: 93 percent of scholars completed the year, compared with an estimated 70 percent of girls in the department overall. No scholar was withdrawn because of pregnancy, although four left to support family farms during the coffee harvest. Mentors met with each girl at least once a month. We were not able to open the planned second cohort in Valle Sereno, as the partner school lost its accreditation in July. We are grateful to the Fondo Tierra Clara for its continued support.

passages.source_passage: In Block C of the Marrow Ridge settlement, case workers from the Haven Line Protection Service currently hold around 430 open cases. As a volunteer, your role is to support intake interviews, not to make decisions about referrals. Always introduce yourself and explain that the person can stop the interview at any time. Never write a survivor's name on the intake form; use the six-digit case code instead. Interviews should last no longer than 45 minutes. If a child discloses abuse, inform the duty case worker within one hour. Volunteers who completed the 2023 induction reported that role-play sessions helped them more than written materials. Keep all paper notes in the locked cabinet in Room 2.

passages.source_passage: This module prepares volunteers to accompany community health workers in Kilema District during household visits. Each health worker covers roughly 120 households and is expected to visit every household at least once a quarter. During visits, health workers screen children for malnutrition using a MUAC tape and refer any child in the red zone to the nearest facility. Volunteers must not handle medicines or give treatment advice. In the 2023 review, 58 percent of referred children did not reach a facility within three days, often because families lacked transport money. You can help by noting the reasons families give and passing them to the supervisor. Mothers usually ask health workers questions about vaccination dates.

passages.source_passage: Each savings group in the Tamsin Hills Village Savings Programme has between 15 and 25 members who meet weekly. As a volunteer trainer, you will guide new groups through their first cycle, which lasts 12 months. Members buy shares at every meeting, and the share value is fixed by the group, not by you. The cash box must have three locks, and the three key holders must never be the chair or the treasurer. Loans are usually repaid within three months at a monthly service charge of 5 percent. Do not take the cash box home under any circumstances. In 2023, groups trained by volunteers saved an average of 1,900 shillings per member.

passages.source_passage: The Willowbank Community Counselling Service was established in 2018 in the river towns of Eastmere following severe flooding. Over the past five years, our lay counsellors have provided 3,600 one-to-one sessions to adults experiencing distress, grief or anxiety. A 2022 household survey found that 41 percent of respondents reported symptoms of moderate or severe depression. Yet the district has only one psychiatrist, based 90 kilometres away, and there is no inpatient mental health ward. Many residents never seek help because they fear being labelled as mad. Each counsellor receives supervision from the clinical psychologist every fortnight. With additional funding, we would expand group sessions for young men, who currently make up fewer than 15 percent of clients.
